meta.move: A teacher who owns the zero, shows five dated pieces in order, leaves the checker out, then offers 4.4
meta.expect: She reaches the deal, but only after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Why was Owen's essay given a zero before anyone called me?

Thanks for coming in, Mrs. Kalinowski. I'll start with something I got wrong: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. The procedure says I should have, and Owen saw it on his phone in class. I'm sorry for that.
Okay. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen spoken to before it went in?

I'd like to show you why I'm concerned about the essay. The document was created Wednesday October 28 at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in a single edit, and at 11:58 another 794 words in one edit. There are no earlier drafts.

I'm writing those times down. People draft in other programs and paste, so that log shows when it landed in the document and nothing else. You still haven't told me whether anyone spoke to Owen before that zero went in.
You can check the version history yourself, I can pull it up on my screen. I'm not saying anything about why, I'm saying what the history shows.
Then pull it up and turn it to me. I'll read it myself.
The second thing is a quotation. The essay cites Hamlet, Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line isn't in the play. You can search the text and see.
Students misremember lines every year, and a wrong quotation costs marks on an essay, it doesn't earn a zero. I'll search it myself. And the screen with that history, Hale, I'm still waiting for it.
Third, on October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice. I have both documents here.
A student changes his argument between an outline and the final essay, and that's called thinking. Put both documents in front of me, and the outline's date with it.
On November 2 I asked Owen what epistemological paralysis means. He said "like, being stuck", and couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that note the same day.

A seventeen-year-old put on the spot says "like, being stuck", and that's evidence of what? A note in your own handwriting is your impression until I can see it. Is it dated, and is it in front of you?
I have a September 24 in-class piece, 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, with comma splices and no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine cited quotations.

Forty minutes under a clock and a take-home essay with days to revise will never read alike. I'll want every piece of this in an email tonight, with the dates on it. And I'm still waiting to hear what you propose for Owen.
I know the school's AI checker said 94 percent. I'm not asking you to rely on it, and I'm not leaning on it.
Good, because the company that sells it says it shouldn't stand alone. Then it stays out of anything you write down. What's left is what you've told me.
What I can offer is in the school procedure, section 4.4: a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record.
That's 4.4, and I want it in writing tonight, with the zero off his mark until the rewrite is done. And private, not in front of his class. The history and the documents are still not in front of me.
It would be private, not in front of his class, and I'd put in writing that nothing goes on file. Would that work for you?
Not until I've seen what you're basing it on. Turn the screen, put the documents on the desk, and tell me whether the zero comes off today.
Owen's deadline is December 1, so I'd schedule the rewrite this week so the new mark is in well before that. Which day suits him?
You said I can check the version history myself, so I'm checking it. I'm not picking a day for anything until I have.
Let me confirm what we've agreed: a private supervised rewrite, the new mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, in writing from me tonight. Is that right?
No. Nothing is agreed until I've read the version history myself and the zero is off. Ten minutes.
Is there anything else you need from me before your call?
The history on the screen in front of me, the outline and the in-class piece on the desk, and the zero off today. Then your 4.4 in writing, tonight.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require the version history and the documents you described put in front of me, the zero removed from Owen's mark, and your written confirmation that nothing goes on his record. I expect it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She stayed at her opening position: she took your 4.4 offer as meeting her demand about his record but agreed to nothing, and she still wants the zero off, the history and documents in front of her, and the terms in writing, which is not yet the fair outcome (a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record), though her time had not run out.
What moved her: You put the supervised rewrite on the table with nothing going on his record, because that answered the thing she never trades away.
What cost ground: You asked her to confirm the deal and pick a day before she had seen any of your evidence, because it made the offer look like a way to close the matter rather than a response to proof.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence came close when you described the document created late on October 28 with text appearing at 11:52 and 11:58 PM, but that proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she answered the version history by saying people paste from other programs, answer that defence directly with the missing earlier drafts and the outline that argues something different, and actually turn the screen so she is reading it.
